About Us
OrbitFX is built and operated by Orbitfx Solution — a Dubai-based financial technology company founded in 2026,
building institutional-grade trading infrastructure for brokers across the Middle East, Asia-Pacific, and beyond. Orbitfx
Solution is the technology company behind OrbitFX, a full-stack brokerage platform serving retail brokers, institutions,
and white-label operators.
The company was founded to solve a clear problem: the brokerage technology market was fragmented, outdated, and
inaccessible to operators who needed a modern, reliable foundation to launch and scale.

Core Architecture
The platform is built on a microservices architecture deployed across geographically redundant data centres. Core
components include the Order Management System (OMS), Risk Engine, Liquidity Aggregator, Trade Reporting
Module, Client Portal, and Chatbot Layer — all communicating over encrypted internal messaging buses with
sub-millisecond latency.

Component Technology Role
Order Management System C++ / FIX Protocol Order routing, matching, lifecycle management
Risk Engine Java / Apache Kafka Real-time P&L, margin, and exposure monitoring
Liquidity Aggregator Python / gRPC Price aggregation from 15+ LP feeds
Client Portal React / Next.js Web-based dashboard for brokers and traders

Reporting Module PostgreSQL / S3 Regulatory and internal trade reporting
Chatbot Layer REST / WebSocket AI chatbot integration for client support

Production Technology Stack (OrbitFX)
• Charting: TradingView Advanced Charts + Lightweight Charts (dual engine)
• Mobile: PWA — installable on iOS & Android, no app store needed
• Real-time: WebSockets for live price ticks, P&L; & position sync
• Security: 2FA + OAuth — Google login, TOTP two-factor authentication
• Permissions: Role-based, 18+ keys, two-gate feature flag control
• Reports: PDF export — statements, trade history & audit log
• Accounts: Multi-account — unlimited LIVE & DEMO per client
• Deployment: Docker — single command deploy, production ready

Key Technical Specifications
• Execution latency: < 1ms order acknowledgement (co-located infrastructure)
• Uptime SLA: 99.9% guaranteed with N+1 redundancy across all critical components
• Security: 256-bit AES encryption at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, ISO 27001 certified
• API protocols: FIX 4.4, FIX 5.0, REST (JSON), WebSocket (streaming prices/trades)
• Data centres: Equinix LD4 (London), NY5 (New York), TY3 (Tokyo); DR in SG1 (Singapore)
• Backup & recovery: RPO < 5 minutes, RTO < 15 minutes

Execution Models
• STP (Straight-Through Processing): orders passed directly to liquidity providers, no dealing desk, no re-quotes
• ECN (Electronic Communications Network): orders matched in a pool of LPs, brokers and institutions; tight
spreads, commission-based pricing
• Market Making: the broker acts as counterparty; fixed spreads available, suited to low-volatility instruments
• DMA (Direct Market Access): for equity CFDs, orders routed directly to the exchange order book with level 2 depth

Margin Call & Stop-Out
A two-stage margin management system is used. When account equity falls to the Margin Call level, the client receives
an automated alert. If equity continues to fall to the Stop-Out level, positions are automatically closed — largest loss
first — to protect the account from negative equity.
Margin Level (%) = (Equity / Used Margin) × 100, where Equity = Balance + Floating P&L.; Example: Balance $1,000,
Used Margin $200, Floating P&L; -$600 → Margin Level = ($1,000-$600)/$200 × 100 = 200%.

Negative Balance Protection
All retail client accounts are protected against negative balances. If a Stop-Out event results in equity going below zero
(e.g. due to extreme slippage in fast markets), the account balance is reset to zero at no charge. This protection does
not apply to professional or institutional accounts unless explicitly stated.

Risk Controls & Alerts
• Email and SMS alerts at configurable margin thresholds (e.g. 200%, 150%, 100%)
• Daily loss limit controls configurable by broker administrators
• Maximum open position limits per instrument and overall
• IP-based login anomaly detection and account lock on suspicious activity
• Real-time exposure dashboard for broker risk desks
• Automatic hedging triggers for correlated position risk

Hedging Policy
Both full and partial hedging are supported. Clients may hold simultaneous long and short positions in the same
instrument; both legs attract margin and swap independently unless netting mode is enabled by the broker.

Regulatory Framework
Orbitfx Solution operates on ISO 27001-compliant infrastructure with full audit trails, penetration testing, and
contractual uptime guarantees. Clients are onboarded only through regulated broker entities. As a technology provider,
the platform supports broker compliance with frameworks including ASIC RG 264, MiFID II/MiFIR, ESMA Guidelines,
SEC/FINRA, ISO 27001, GDPR (EU), SOC 2 Type II logging, and FATF Recommendations.

Trust Center Highlights
• ISO 27001 Compliant — information security management certified across all production infrastructure
• SOC 2 Type II Logging — full audit trail and access logging aligned with SOC 2 operational standards
• GDPR Data Practices — client data handling policies aligned with GDPR for EU-facing broker operations
• 99.9% Uptime SLA — contractual uptime guarantees backed by multi-region failover and monitoring
• Penetration Testing — bi-annual third-party penetration testing with published remediation reports
• Responsible Disclosure — public vulnerability disclosure programme; report security issues to
security@OrbitFXSolution.com (48-hour response)

KYC / AML Requirements

• Automated sanctions screening against UN, OFAC, EU, and UK lists on onboarding and ongoing basis
• Real-time AML engine flags unusual patterns including structuring, layering, and rapid fund movement
• Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) filed with the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) of Sri Lanka as required

17. Glossary of Terms
Ask — The price at which you can buy an instrument. Also called the offer price.
Bid — The price at which you can sell an instrument.
CFD — Contract for Difference — an agreement to exchange the difference in value of an asset from open to close.
ECN — Electronic Communications Network — a system that matches buy and sell orders from multiple participants.
Equity — Account balance plus or minus any floating (unrealised) profit or loss on open positions.
FIX Protocol — Financial Information eXchange — the industry standard messaging format for financial transactions.

17. Glossary of Terms
Hedging — Holding opposite positions in the same instrument to reduce directional exposure.
KYC — Know Your Customer — the process of verifying client identity before onboarding.
g. 1:100).
Liquidity — The ease with which an asset can be bought or sold without significantly affecting its price.
Lot — A standardised unit of trade. 1 standard lot = 100,000 units of base currency in FX.
Margin — The amount of capital required to open and maintain a leveraged trading position.

17. Glossary of Terms
Margin Call — A notification when account equity falls to a defined percentage of used margin, warning the trader to
add funds or reduce positions.
MT4 / MT5 — MetaTrader 4 / 5 — popular third-party trading platforms often integrated with broker platforms.
Pip — Percentage in Point — the smallest standard price movement. 0001.
Requote — When a broker offers a different price than initially requested due to fast-moving markets.
Rollover / Swap — The overnight interest charge or credit applied to positions held past the daily cut-off (22:00 GMT).

17. Glossary of Terms
SLA — Service Level Agreement — a defined commitment for uptime, response, and resolution times.
Slippage — The difference between the expected trade price and the actual execution price in fast markets.
Spread — The difference between the Bid and Ask price.
STP — Straight-Through Processing — orders are passed directly to LPs without dealing desk intervention.
Stop-Out — Automatic closure of positions when account equity falls below a set margin percentage threshold.

17. Glossary of Terms
Swap-Free Account — An account type where overnight swap charges are replaced by an administration fee,
common for Islamic finance compliance.
Trailing Stop — A dynamic stop-loss order that moves with the market price by a fixed distance to lock in profits.
White-Label — A fully branded platform provided by the technology partner but operating under the client broker's own
brand identity.
